questions.text: What can a person do with a document?
questions.assumed: View or edit; being able to edit includes being able to view.

questions.text: Who can share or unshare a document?

questions.assumed: No: teams contain people only; nested teams come later.

questions.text: Do folders nest, and does sharing a folder share everything inside it?
questions.assumed: Yes to both: folders form a tree, a document is in at most one folder, and a share of a folder covers everything inside it, at any depth.

questions.text: What is out of scope for the first version?
questions.assumed: Consistency snapshots (versions), deny rules, expiring shares, audit logs and outside identity providers.

questions.text: Can a share end at a time, and what happens then?
questions.assumed: A share may carry an end time; from then on it reaches no one, whether or not a job has run (access reads the clock); a job every minute removes ended shares; sharing again replaces the time.

questions.text: Can someone be invited, and does an invitation give access before it is accepted?
questions.assumed: An invitation names a person and a level, gives no access until accepted, lapses after 7 days, and any editor can withdraw it; accepting it makes the share.

questions.text: What does deleting a document do?
questions.assumed: It goes to the trash for 30 days, where its shares give no access; an editor can restore it, and its shares hold again; after 30 days a job deletes it and its shares for good.
The server's clock in seconds, read once per request, never going back; jobs run every minute, one at a time with the requests.

questions.text: Moving a document out of a folder can take away the mover's own access. Allowed?
May the last edit share of a document be unshared?
Access requests. Who can ask, and who answers?
questions.assumed: Anyone named in the library asks for view or edit on a document or folder; any editor of it approves or declines; a reminder to the editors after 48 h; declined automatically after 7 days; approving makes the share.

questions.text: Notifications. What is notified, and what if delivery fails?
questions.assumed: Invitations, accepted invitations, access requests and their answers, and shares ending within a day; through an outbox, retried until delivered, at least once and never twice for one event (idempotent by event id).

Every document has exactly one owner (its creator); only the owner transfers it, to someone who may edit it; the owner always may edit; an owner leaving a team keeps their documents; the owner's share cannot be unshared or expire.

Every change (share, unshare, move, invite, accept, withdraw, trash, restore, purge, transfer) is logged with who, what and when; every yes of canView is traceable to the log entries of the shares that gave it; the log is append-only and kept for a year.

questions.text: Failures. What does a client see when the store fails mid-request?
questions.assumed: The request fails with 503 and changes nothing (one transaction per request); a failed housekeeping run is retried at the next minute and changes nothing until it succeeds.
